NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE shows a street-facing elevation with a stepped brick frontage, a two-storey dark panel zone, two stacked glass balconies, a narrow four-part window strip, raised three-bay glazing beneath a thin roof edge, and a recessed entrance behind brick boundary walls and metal gates. CURRENT preserves this overall arrangement, but the entrance doors are oversized and the narrow window strip has incorrect width and subdivisions. SOURCE does not establish rear elevations, building depth or concealed roof construction; those CURRENT regions cannot be judged for fidelity. Screenshots alone do not establish concealed assembly joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: CURRENT entrance doors nearly fill the central opening and read as a broad, subdivided screen. SOURCE shows a substantially narrower pair of doors within a dark recessed porch.
action: Locally narrow the door assembly, restore two leaves and the surrounding recessed reveals, and preserve the existing entrance opening and balcony above.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT right-hand window strip is roughly one-fifth narrower relative to the brick frontage. Its central vertical mullion continues through all four glazed sections; SOURCE shows that division in the upper pair, with undivided lower panes.
action: Widen the strip locally while retaining its approximate centerline and vertical extent. Remove the central mullion from the lower two sections and retain the substantial dark separator between the upper and lower pairs.</issue>
<keep>Seven vertical bays across the dark two-storey panel zone.
Two stacked balconies, with the lower balcony wider than the upper.
Three glazing bays across the exposed top of the raised glazed volume.</keep>
